notes.title: Promise Mascot Agency's new update just made it even weirder, and tougher
notes.notes:
Some games really leave you feeling like you're in a fever dream, and Promise Mascot Agency falls perfectly into that category. One of the most random, jarring, yet brilliant open-world RPGs around, it combines all manner of genre influences and surreal character designs to create something totally unique. Now, it's cranking the weirdness up another notch, because thanks to a free update, you can grind your trusty kei truck on rails like you're in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater.

notes.title: Promise Mascot Agency, the weirdest game of 2025, is finally out on Steam
notes.notes:
Once upon a time I only played triple-A games. Devil May Cry, Dragon Age, Mortal Kombat; all amazing franchises in their own rights, each of which defined my childhood in many different ways. But, since I began working in this industry - and at PCGamesN specifically - I've fallen in love with indie games, happily casting aside big open-world, narrative-driven triple-A games for gems like Animal Well, Indika, and, now, Promise Mascot Agency. Easily one of the weirdest games I've ever encountered, it's become my most-played game of 2025 almost overnight. I absolutely have a problem, but I'm very okay with it.

notes.title: Promise Mascot Agency review
notes.notes: The thing you need to understand about the world is that it's run by money. Absent normal signifiers of human society, absent any semblance of structure or narrative that makes sense, this is a truth that remains. Promise Mascot Agency is a game that understands this, among other fundamental truths of the world, like how the blood of the covenant is thicker than the water of the womb and how an unchallenged incumbent mayor in a town that people mostly leave is a destructive force rivaled only by natural disasters and anonymous internet commenters. At its core, Promise Mascot Agency is a fanged ode to the responsibilities of civic life, to bureaucratic idleness and indulgence, and to the numbers going up at the center of it all. It is brutally funny, brutally mercenary, and brutally good... Read more.

notes.title: Meet Tanukin!
notes.notes:
🎨Designed by: Ikumi Nakamura & Mai Mattori
🎨Rendered by: Inko Ai Takita

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/8caadf3ae9a1f798243f684df8d801871879e957.png[/img]

Tanukin is a mascot that lives within a grand delusion of his own making. He believes that he is an ancient warlord, and he is very confused by the modern world. His only desire in life is to conquer a castle fit for a great warlord of his (believed) stature, where he will rule for the rest of his days. 

On his journey, Michi’s patience will be put to the test dealing with all the various mascot related mayhem, and none will push him to the limit more than the headstrong Tanukin! 

[b]Developer notes: [/b]
I really like Tanukin’s design. He communicates so much about himself with just a single glance at him. For a while, I wasn’t entirely sure how to write him, but without revealing too much, his Life Satisfaction quest was really fun to write and I always get a chuckle out of Michi’s attitude at the end of it.
[i][b]Oli Clarke Smith, Game Director
[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/0736c78506f6f081008bb19ae82c8b8839dd36a4.png[/img]

notes.title: Meet Koke-Maru!
notes.notes:
🎨Designed by: Ikumi Nakamura & Mai Mattori
🎨Rendered by: Inko Ai Takita
🎨3D by: Rachel Noy

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/5eef191e998905dc761e51dc404a36fa734aa13d.png[/img]

No job. All vibes. Koke-Maru is a marimo moss ball creature that just hangs around in the rice fields and baths, keeping moist and staying out of the limelight. They have the power to magically craft objects, they can also turn invisible. Don’t ask how or why. But this has led some scumbags to try to harvest his mossy body, believing it has ‘godly powers’. 

Koke-Maru has lived in the town for their entire life, but an incident many years ago caused him to go deep into hiding. But when Michi and Pinky☆ offer them a role at the agency, Koke-Maru jumps at the chance to work with others and make some new, sentient friends.

[b]Developer notes:[/b]
I like Koke because he just wants to do his thing and chill. He doesn't want to be bothered, he just wants to focus on his craft. HIGHLY RELATABLE.
[i][b]Oli Clarke Smith, Game Director[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/bcf9d424886fb45780726a9816956afb6481f351.png[/img]

notes.title: Meet Karoushi!
notes.notes:
🎨Designed by: Ikumi Nakamura, Mai Mattori, Inko Ai Takita & Rachel Noy
🎨Rendered by: Inko Ai Takita
🎨3D by: Pav Plaha

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/99de255a2c3714af1ebf3b87da3e516763335f0a.png[/img]

It’s rare to find someone in Kaso-Machi that hasn’t heard the legends about the haunted abandoned tunnel outside of town. Sometimes described as a ghost, for others, they swear whatever haunts the tunnel is the Grim Reaper himself. In reality, it’s just a very tired boy called Karoushi, who happens to exist in the space between life and death, and can commune with the spirits of Kaso-Machi. No big deal. 

Karoushi is a cautionary tale of burnout. He teaches about the danger of overworking yourself for any corporation, and empowers workers to stand up for their rights. Ultimately, he wants everyone to enjoy the life they have, while they have it, lest they end up bitter and alone like he is. 

[b]Developer notes:[/b] 
I gave him his weird room in the haunted tunnel because I loved the creepiness of Highway Star’s tunnel room in Jojo Part 4.
[i][b]Oli Clarke Smith, Game Director[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/c63bd23cfcdfe304ed0480793a62afb2d21035a8.png[/img]

notes.title: Meet Kabaya King!
notes.notes:
🎨Designed by: Ikumi Nakamura and Mai Mattori
🎨Rendered by: Inko Ai Takita
🎨3D by: Pav Plaha

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/f9ef69291b3fb16b153337555ef35522cfe6e8a6.png[/img]

An eel mascot going through a bit of an existential crisis. Previously employed to promote unagi bowls, but he doesn’t want to do this anymore due to the endangerment of Japanese eels, we love a sustainable king!  

He now passionately advocates for respecting all the living creatures that we eat and conservation in general. 

All of his favourite things begin with the letter ‘U’, maybe linked to the fact that during summer in Japan, some people like to eat food that begins with ‘u’ in the belief that it helps with the heat. 

[b]Developer notes: [/b]
Kabaya King is one of my favourite mascot designs in the game, visually. He's cute in some regards but his abdomen is horrifying.
[i][b]Oli Clarke Smith, Game Director[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/614e5da5f1a69a082b617e01640b6f47c18febb8.png[/img]

notes.title: Meet Neko Roll！
notes.notes:
🎨Designed by: Ikumi Nakamura + Mai Mattori
🎨Rendered by: Inko Ai Takita
🎨3D by: Pav Plaha

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/f4abf661a9dfcd00a45381a161191952d58fbaaa.png[/img]

Neko Roll got damn sick of doing tea ceremonies for tourists in Kyoto and came to Kaso-Machi for a fresh start. While she visually presents as a traditional cutesy mascot, she wants to rebel against being type-cast and limited by her looks. There is more to her than being cute you know! 

Neko Roll wants to do fun events and not be limited by the mascot industry in Kyoto. She also wants to save up enough money to buy a tea farm and Kaso-Machi has an abandoned farm that would be perfect. 

Cats seem to be drawn to this town as it almost exists in a kind of spiritual limbo. Whenever something spooky is happening, you can bet there’ll be a cat nearby. Meow. 

[b]Developer notes:[/b]
Neko Roll is such a sweetheart. When we got the concept back there was a note attached to it, saying “she meows when you poke the sponge part” and we thought that was so cute. Sometimes mascots just need to be cute.

Back in the day, Ichigo used to be THE model for chocolate adverts, he was very much a Big Deal(™), and was the ubiquitous face of Valentine’s Day and White Day. One day he reached his limit and had enough of showbiz, so he finally decided to chase his dreams and buy a farm. His farm is struggling due to the high price his premium strawberries carry and the lack of tourists in town. 

Michi and Pinky convince him to work with them despite Ichigo’s doubts at being associated with a yakuza. 

Mr. Love wants to use the money he earns from mascot work to fund modernising his farm, buying more eco-friendly equipment and starting to freeze dry his strawberries so he can ship them out of this remote town. Can you help him succeed in his agricultural dream? 

[b]Developer notes: [/b]
Ichi was designed by our art director, Rachel, as we wanted to get some cuter mascots in the game. We didn’t want to just make a sweet and cute mascot however, we decided to give him a tough edge which we had great fun with when writing his story.
We had a shiba inu at the beginning of development before she sadly passed away, and it just felt wrong not to have a shiba mascot in the game.

Natsukatshii was the absolute queen of mascots in the Shōwa era. She was a national celebrity and rose to huge heights of stardom. Now in her twilight years, she has retired to Kaso-Machi to live quietly, bringing a nostalgic air of old time glamour with her.  

She has found a new purpose in town, now making delicious cakes and sweets in Mieko’s café. She offers to work with Michi after seeing how he has welcomed all sorts of mascots into his agency, and offers mentorship to the younger mascots like To-Fu. notes.title: Meet Kaso-Koumori!
notes.notes:
🎨Designed by: Rachel Noy & Oli Clarke Smith
🎨Rendered by: Inko Ai Takita
🎨3D by: Gaby Wilde

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/05f0e691fd76ef6f5ac403a9063f66074e83097e.png[/img]

Kaso-Koumori is supposed to be the town’s official mascot, but it turns out he was only being used by the mayor in order to secure a grant (damn that crusty old geezer 😡) and was left out to dry.  Very soon after arriving in town, he realised that he actually wouldn’t be getting any work, and worse than that, was stuck there with no way to leave! The worst! He even changed his name to fit in with the town, which just goes to show that no good deed goes unpunished.

💮As Michi begins exploring the town, he finds that a long forgotten stamp rally is still operational. Kaso-Koumori can be seen on the stamp card, and the stamp itself, one poignant reminder of his very short-lived stint as a town mascot. 

🦇Kaso-Koumori can be found hanging out at the mines most of the time, he’s big into bats and is desperate to hang out with them. This of course has nothing to do with him possibly (definitely) having a total complex about his always-on head lamp annoying everyone. Which it totally doesn’t, but he won’t be told. Okay maybe it annoys the bats. But that’s IT. 
If you don’t like bats. I’m going to stop you right there, Kaso-Koumori has nothing to say to you. 

[b]Developer notes: [/b]
Kaso-Koumori came about when we began to imagine what kind of a mascot the mayor would hire for the town after his bad experience with Pinky☆. Kaso-Koumori is pretty much her opposite, quiet, reserved and easy to manipulate. Unfortunately the perfect prey for a crusty old geezer… 
[i][b]Rachel Noy, Art Director[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/e40c6cc40b595f7522a94dabd905f649e66cc2af.png[/img]

We know what you’re thinking, and no, it’s not that. It’s actually yam juice! Being covered in yam all the time proves to be a real blocker on career progression, as he could only find work promoting yam to the town's elderly population. This happy go lucky cat hasn’t let this stop him though.  

📹He is obsessed with adult video, and has dreams of working in the AV industry to promote the responsible and ethical consumption of the genre. He wears his interests on his sleeves, and has no shame about his hobbies - good for you Trororo! 
If there is one thing he hates though, it’s pixelation. Nothing irks him more, why is that there anyway? GET RID OF IT! 

😻With bundles of sincere, slightly rebellious energy, Trororo wants to help Michi and everyone else in town be more confident in their interests, all while achieving his own dream of being the mascot for an adult video industry that protects and respects its workers 

[b]Developer notes:[/b]
His name was bestowed upon him by Nakamura-san and is a mix of tororo (yam) and troll as he wants to troll the censors. His design and name are of course based on the Japanese, sticky grated yam, which is often served on rice. Yummmmm

notes.title: Meet To-Fu!
notes.notes:
🎨Designed by: Ikumi Nakamura & Mai Mattori
🎨Rendered by: Inko Ai Takita
🎨3D by: Rachel Noy

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/9c4e2661dbf3f55e7cfe6f0c4b1b4f0a736c4fca.png[/img]

To-Fu is a beautiful, sensitive soul, trying to survive in a cruel world. He tries his best, but he often finds himself completely overwhelmed by….literally anything and everything. He doesn’t really understand why he cries all the time, but he knows he can’t stop 😭

🫸At school, To-Fu was bullied badly. An easy target who couldn’t stand up for himself, he resigned himself to being a victim. But he found a friend and protector for life in his classmate Pinky☆. We know that if there is one thing Pinky☆ hates, it’s a bully (and crusty old geezers, but mostly bullies), so she took it upon herself to stand up for To-Fu and throw hands (fingers?), at anyone who dared be mean to her friend. 

To-Fu is the first mascot that comes to see Pinky☆ and Michi after hearing that the agency has reopened. He is being very brave, and following the advice of his therapist, who has told him that he should try pushing himself to try new things. 

Will he be able to achieve his dream of becoming firm and strong? Or will he learn to accept that he is a soft, silken tofu boy? Help this sweet boy on his road to success and self love! 

[b]Developer notes:[/b]
To-Fu was actually the very first mascot that got modelled for the game. Poor old To-Fu has been the test case for everything. He has seen all of the horrors that game development has to offer, so there really has been no respite for this sweet silken boy. 

I especially like To-Fu because the first game I really fell in love with was Resident Evil 2. That game was directed by Hideki Kamiya and featured a block of tofu as an unlockable character. Kamiya-san then worked with Nakamura-san and she designed To-Fu so it feels like he connects me back to my first video game love. 
[i][b]Oli Clarke Smith, Game Director[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/c0284ab064d35b6d2bfffaa121e4f0110d2f50a4.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/39bdca61dc9b48e928299c24812a2fabdfcf9529.png[/img]

Pinky☆ is angry. Shunned by a world that doesn’t think a severed pinky-finger is ‘conventionally cute’, a world that can’t appreciate her passion for violence, and worst of all, a world that doesn’t respect mascots. She has a small but fierce circle of friends in town, most of whom she’s helped out of a tight spot (she will do LITERALLY ANYTHING for her pals), but her mischief and superstar personality have proven too much for some townsfolk to handle.

She is the original owner of the mascot agency business, entrusted to her by Matriarch Shimazu, but it soon became clear her strengths lay elsewhere. So her business licence was soon revoked by Mayor Maeda (a crusty old geezer who can’t take a joke) after an unfortunate incident at the mayor’s granddaughter’s birthday party. As a last resort, Pinky converted the agency into a love hotel to keep a roof over her head. A severed finger has to do what she has to do! 

When Michi moves into town to take over the business, he is super lucky to have Pinky☆ become his assistant manager (he’d be lost without her 💖) With Michi having to come to terms with operating in a civilian space post-yakuza, and Pinky☆ just needing someone to take a chance on her, together these unlikely besties help each other navigate the world, and fulfil their dreams ✨

[b]Developer Insights:[/b]
Michi is a fish very quickly out of water in the game, so we needed a character that would be a guide for players throughout their journey. When we asked our artists to design us a mascot assistant to work with Michi, we knew we wanted her to have big Pop Team Epic and Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken! Energy, so that was the main inspiration for her design. 

The idea of the character that almost ends up completing Michi and complementing him so well, being a severed finger, after he had to cut off his own in atonement for his actions, was something that we really loved and felt profound.  With this in mind, our art director, Rachel really strongly established the theme of characters keeping pinky promises to each other. We knew we wanted the game to be about chasing dreams, no matter who or what you are, and keeping promises naturally fed into that. 

Pinky☆ is my favourite character to write. She’s witty and sarcastic, but she means well and has so much heart. She teases Michi constantly, but would do anything to support him. Pinky☆ is one of those people that just needs an opportunity and some support to achieve great things.

[i][b]Oli Clarke Smith, Game Director[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/40e54edd95f140a29be5091e7d662c12535694c1.png[/img]

notes.title: Michi
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45000200/7403fa77664271a8b896f643b105ca1c7cea13c7.png[/img]

Michi grew up in a well-to-do family but rebelled against his parent’s pressure and fell into delinquency. After becoming a gang leader, he almost met his end when he stubbornly fought against some new rivals despite knowing he’d lose. The ensuing brawl left him bleeding out in the rain.

Having earned something of a reputation in Fukuoka for his fearlessness and recklessness, Matriarch Shimazu scooped him off the street. From that day, he swore an oath to his new boss dedicating himself to her service. Working in the Shimazu Family gave him purpose and familial bonds he had never experienced before. He managed to learn to control himself with her teachings, but the reputation of his past as “The Demon of Fukuoka” still follows him.

Michi got the nickname of ‘The Janitor’ because he always cleans up any problem his family has and leaves a scene spotless. Upon entering the Family, his first job was cleaning the office, and sweeping became a distraction to calm his mind. Later, his broom became his weapon as it’s inconspicuous, an extension of his body feared by anyone that crossed the Shimazu Family.

Michi is completely loyal to his new family, almost to a fault as he chooses his family over money in a deal gone wrong, a decision that plummets the Shimazu Family into a difficult situation. Instead of killing Michi as most yakuza bosses would, Shimazu fakes Michi’s death and sends him somewhere she knows no yakuza would dare to follow him.

Michi now finds himself in a dying town, hunted by a yakuza killing curse. He has been ripped from the life he knew and is struggling to find his way in a strange new world of mascot management. He is a man of duty and he will not let his Matriarch’s dream die, even if it kills him.

[b]Developer Insight:[/b]
Michi, like a lot of our characters, was designed by Ikumi Nakamura and Mai Mattori. We asked them to design Michi with only a few key points, and the rest was left up to them. We were pleasantly surprised by a yakuza wearing sandals, a track jacket and carrying a broom. We loved how unique he was and how his appearance immediately told a story.

We can’t wait for you to get to know Michi!

notes.title: A Halloween Interview with Pinky☆!
notes.notes:
We met Pinky☆ for an interview on our recent visit to Promise Mascot Agency, a mascot-for-hire agency ran out of what is seemingly an old and decrepit love hotel. Don’t let looks deceive you however, Pinky☆’s here and she means business! She may be in the gutter but she’s reaching for the stars!

We chatted to Pinky over a cup of tea, once she’d finished smashing all of the dirty cups in the small kitchenette and swearing about her good for nothing janitor. We didn’t drink our tea.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45000200/402b29b00c1fa2281957dfa7aaccfa380c56dcf1.png[/img]

[b]Interviewer:[/b]
I’ve never conducted an interview on a spinning bed before, this is a new experience! I wonder if you’d like to introduce yourself and your company?

[b]Pinky☆:[/b]
I find rotating beds help clear the mind. There’s nothing like imagining the awful things that have been done on it to make you thankful for the life you’re leading.

Anyway, I’m Pinky☆! I’m the assistant manager of the Promise Mascot Agency. The manager can’t speak to the press because he’s dead. Kind of. Don’t worry about him.


[b]Interviewer:[/b]
So we hear that you were once one of the biggest mascots in this town, arguably even in Fukuoka. What caused you to shun the spotlight and want to go behind the scenes?

[b]Pinky☆:[/b]
I didn’t want to go behind the scenes, the goddamn mayor forced me to! That crusty old geezer got all pissy when I didn’t perform well at his granddaughter’s birthday party. The mascot business was going poorly due to factors OUTSIDE OF MY CONTROL, and I was the only mascot left. So I had to do the event for His Majesty. I’m not a people person. Things were said that shouldn’t have been said. A knife was brandished when it shouldn’t have been.

Unregardlessly, we’re back in business, and I’m going to suffocate the life out of the mayor, if it's the last thing I do.


[b]Interviewer: [/b]
How do you feel about Kaso-Machi? What are the local specialities and why should people come to visit?
[b]Pinky☆:[/b]
Kaso-Machi is wonderful, if you like dying towns and curses! We don’t have a lot here, but we do have mountain nightmare spirits, a really handsome mechanic, my grandma’s coffee shop AND an S&M dungeon!

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45000200/acfb4b5fcd5a109d8a0d778c89732bbc2d4023b0.png[/img]

[b]
Interviewer:[/b]
If this is an abandoned, haunted town, why do you think your business will be successful here? Surely a town with no tourism doesn’t have a great need for mascots?

[b]Pinky☆:[/b]
Well, for a start, we don’t have a lot of choice. For reasons I am not at liberty to discuss, if we don’t make this place a success, some people are going to die. To that end, me and the boss are working to rejuvenate this town ourselves. The crusty old mayor hasn’t been spending the government money to revive the town, so we’re pouring what little we have back into the town.

The boss is all about helping people achieve their dreams, even if it is a total pain in the ass, so we’re helping them rebuild their businesses. We’re doing it out of the goodness of our hearts AND to get a cut of the profits when the tourists come. Create the world you want to live in. Or something.

[b]Interviewer:[/b]
Are you doing anything special for Halloween?
[b]Pinky☆:[/b]
Buddy, it’s always Halloween in this town.

We’ve got bat mascots, an eel mascot with his stomach split open, a mascot that might be a ghost, and two mascot brothers that think they’re gods. Not to mention the weird cult that meets in a cave, and the door to another dimension in the hills. Oh yeah, there’s the ghost at the train station as well. If you like the occult, we’ve got you covered.

[b]Interviewer:[/b]
In a world full of colourful and cute mascots, what do you think is the biggest charm of the mascots at Promise Mascot Agency?
[Might be good to mention here how they are all misfits but they recruit mascots being themselves so clients get something fresh]
[b]Pinky☆:[/b]
All of our mascots are misfits. We’re not like those lame mainstream mascots. All of our mascots have a unique charm. It might be tempting to call it a freakshow, but that goes against our HR policies, so let’s just say that we provide mascots for events that you won’t find anywhere else.

[b]
Interviewer:[/b]
What makes Promise Mascot Agency unique, and what can you offer customers that other mascot agencies can’t?

[b]Pinky☆:[/b]
Well, we’re desperate so we’re relatively cheap. And degenerates online loves seeing weirdos fail, and we can provide that by the bucket load.

“PINKY☆!”

Sorry, that was the boss. He’s really uptight about me speaking to the press. We’ll have to blur him out of the photo.


[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45000200/6e7e1155f9a0f66310e6df6141f2f224b7b61ee6.png[/img]

[b]Interviewer:[/b]
What are the goals for Promise Mascot Agency and its mascots?

[b]Pinky☆:[/b]
TO MAKE HELL OF MONEY AND NOT DIE!

That’s number 1. Number 2 is to crush all other mascot agencies under our boot. In doing so, we will help all of our mascots achieve their dreams. So long as their dreams aren’t too time consuming.

Listen, I was abandoned by my dad, the mayor ruined my business, and lots of people think I’m a joke. The boss needs to atone for a mistake and save his family or whatever, but let me tell you something, if it helps make this agency a success, I will do something worth atoning for. You feel me?

[b]Interviewer:[/b]
What do you like and hate about your job?

[b]Pinky☆:[/b]
I like not having to run a love hotel anymore. People make me sick. I also like being driven around by the boss so we can meet all my friends. Hey, you ever been to Bar Itai? Mama-san’s good people. I’m also having a lot of fun antagonising the mayor. I think we’re pretty close to giving him a heart attack.

I hate how poor the people in this town are. Like, why do we have to work so goddarn hard to get paid? I’m in the prime of my life, I shouldn’t be busting my hump so much with this.

[b]
Interviewer:[/b]
What do you like to do on your time off?

[b]Pinky☆:[/b]
Before reopening the agency, me and Shiori, one of our employees, used to enjoy doing shakedowns on the pervs visiting the love hotel. Nowadays, I don’t get a lot of time off. Making dreams come true doesn’t leave me with a lot of downtime. I’m forced to selflessly devote myself to other people.


[b]Interviewer:[/b]
Anything else you’d like to add?

[b]Pinky☆:[/b]
Please come to Kaso-Machi, open a business, and hire our mascots for all of your promotional events! If you don’t, I want to know what your goddamn problem is.

[[i]A voice from another room shouts[/i]] “PINKY☆!”


[b]Anonymous sign-off comment from the mysterious owner:[/b]
Thank you for your support. We endeavour to provide mascots that entertain and delight. We’re looking forward to doing business with you.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45000200/9ae1e9213b450de73d6db81735af15461306afd5.png[/img]

Thank you, Pinky☆ and the mysterious owner!
we’re looking forward to doing business with you too.

“Be the boss. Turn a profit. Recruit and manage a chaotic roster of magnificent Mascots” 

Promise Mascot Agency is due for release in 2025! [b]Available to wishlist now![/b]

notes.title: The First Promise Mascot Agency Interview!
notes.notes:
Last week we had a lovely big chat with Katelyn Mitchell Jewett of Gamerant about all things PROMISE MASCOT AGENCY! Topics include inspirations for the game, working with Ikumi Nakamura, our favourite mascots and more! 

[url=https://gamerant.com/promise-mascot-agency-interview-ikumi-nakamura-mascots-mystery-yakuza/]Click here to read! It’s a great article![/url]

We’ve got more interviews and announcements on the horizon, so keep an eye out! We can’t wait to share more of Kaso-Machi with you. Thanks again to Katelyn! 

And thanks again to everyone else, too - we continue to be blown away by the reaction to Promise Mascot Agency. Developing a game for four years, you worry how people will react to it when you finally show them. We hoped that people would watch the trailer and want to know more - but the huge amount of excitement, hype and willingness to go with us on this bizarre journey was more than we could have ever expected. That’s the stuff that keeps us going, and seeing people continue to discover the game with variations of “I don’t know what this is, but it looks awesome” is heartwarming.

We’ve seen incredible reception not just from fans but also the press - here are a few of our favourites:

[i]“One of the recruitable misfit mascots in the trailer, a large block of tofu with tears constantly streaming down its face, does battle with a normal-sized door by trying to walk through it. The tofu loses. "Currently soft but wants to be firm" is noted on Tofu's character sheet. This is the best combat I've seen in a game all year.”[/i]
Wes Fenlon, PC Gamer

[i]“Look, I understand that some level of objectivity and reservation is part of the post, but I no longer care. Promise Mascot Agency is the videogame singularity. It contains all good things about all videogames and once it’s out, I will not need to ever play another videogame again, which is good, because no-one will dare to make another videogame after it.”[/i]
Nic Reuben, Rock Paper Shotgun

[i]“It looks spectacular. I reviewed Paradise Killer way back when it was released. It was one of my favorite games of that year, and has stuck with me since. You probably could have struck my interest with “from the developers of Paradise Killer,” but the trailer delivers beyond that with just a feverish representation of Japan. Damn, I’m excited.”[/i]
Zoey Handley, Destructoid
